sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team queries — find direct reports; department: filtering by department; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type; is_active: filtering active policies only; leave_type, is_active: combined filter for active policies of a given type

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups by employee — my requests; status: filtering by status (pending approvals, etc.); leave_policy_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager approval history; employee_id, status: combined filter — employee's requests by status

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups by employee — my balances; leave_policy_id: filtering by policy; fiscal_year: filtering by fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite for one balance row per employee/policy/year; employee_id, fiscal_year: employee's balances for a given year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookup audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering by action type

data_notes: Five conceptual tables defined: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. Five repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool. Two open questions recorded: used_days computation strategy (derived vs stored counter) and day granularity (whole vs half-day vs hourly). The leave_requests table references leave_policies (not a separate leave_types table) since the DOMAIN.md defines LeaveType as an enum on LeavePolicy.leave_type. The audit_logs table satisfies GP-002 for all state-changing operations across the leave module.

open_questions.question: How is used_days on leave_balances computed — is it derived live from approved leave_requests (SUM of day counts where status=APPROVED) or is it a stored counter incremented/decremented on approval/rejection/cancellation?
open_questions.impact: Affects consistency guarantees: derived is always accurate but slower; stored counter risks drift but is fast. Also affects whether balance recalculation jobs are needed.
candidate_options: Derived: compute used_days via SUM query on leave_requests at read time
Stored counter: increment on APPROVED, decrement on CANCELLED/REJECTED (if previously approved)
Hybrid: stored counter with periodic reconciliation job

open_questions.question: Are leave days always whole days, or does the system need to support half-day or hourly leave requests?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether used_days/remaining_days are integers or decimals, and whether date columns need time components. Affects overlap detection logic and balance deduction precision.
candidate_options: Whole days only: start_date and end_date are date-only; day count = (end_date - start_date) + 1
Half-day support: add a half_day flag or allow fractional day counts
Hourly: store start_datetime and end_datetime with hour precision
